crm.title: CRM Integration
crm.description: Send call data to your CRM after each call. Configure server URL and authentication.
crm.enableDesc: When enabled, call data will be sent to your CRM system after each call ends.
crm.durationHint: How duration and talk time are sent. In seconds mode the keys become durationInSeconds / talkTimeInSeconds, so the receiver cannot misread the unit.
crm.keyNamesHint: Rename any field to the key your CRM expects. Leave blank to use the default.
crm.collisionWarn: Two fields would be sent under the same key ({{keys}}). The duplicate rename is dropped and the field keeps its default key.
crm.outcomeMapHint: Remap an outcome to what your CRM expects (e.g. BUSY → NO_ANSWER). Applies to both status and disposition. Leave blank to send unchanged.
crm.connectionSub: Where OpDesk reaches your CRM and how it authenticates.
crm.verifySSLDesc: Turn off only for a CRM using a self-signed certificate.
crm.blockPrivateDesc: Loopback and cloud-metadata are always blocked. Enable only if your CRM is public — it rejects on-prem/LAN URLs.
crm.deliverySub: When a call ends, where the record goes and which calls qualify.
crm.syncOffNote: Call-data sync is paused — no call records are pushed. The connection above stays configured.
crm.syncEndpointHint: Appended to the server URL. Leave blank to use the connection endpoint path.
crm.noDirections: No direction selected — nothing will be pushed.
crm.payloadSub: Choose the values to send and, if needed, the key each one lands under.
crm.noCatalog: The field catalog could not be loaded. Reload the page and try again.
crm.slashWarn: The endpoint path has no leading slash — it is joined to the server URL exactly as shown above.
crm.previewPaused: Call-data sync is paused — nothing is pushed.
crm.previewEmpty: No fields selected — the CRM would receive an empty body.
crm.previewHintAll: Example values — pushed after every call.
crm.previewHintNone: Example values. No direction is selected, so nothing is pushed.
crm.previewHintSome: Example values — pushed after every {{dirs}} call.
crm.lookupSub: Resolve caller numbers to CRM contact names, shown on the softphone and dashboards. Results are cached server-side.
crm.lookupOffNote: Contact lookup is off — calls show bare numbers. The connection above stays configured.
crm.lookupUrlHint: Appended to the server URL. [Number] is replaced with the caller’s number; without it, ?phone=[Number] is added automatically.
crm.lookupNameTemplateHint: Each [path] is a dot/index path into the JSON response (data.0.name reads response.data[0].name). Multiple paths are joined, e.g. first + last name.
crm.lookupMatchDigitsHint: Caching and verification compare only the last N digits, so +20…, 0020… and 0… match the same contact. 0 = full number.
crm.lookupVerifyPathHint: Path to the phone field of the returned record. A result only counts when it matches the searched number — protects against fuzzy-search false positives.
crm.lookupTtlHint: How long a "no match" answer is remembered before the CRM is asked about that number again. Matched contacts are saved to the phonebook permanently.
crm.lookupTestNoMatch: The CRM answered, but no name was extracted. Check the name template against the response below.

mobileWake.title: Mobile Wake
mobileWake.description: Wake a closed mobile softphone for incoming calls (RFC 8599). The phone puts its push token in its SIP REGISTER; OpDesk pushes it, holds the call until it re-registers, then lets it ring.
mobileWake.enabledHint: Before an extension with a push binding is dialed, push it and hold the call while the app wakes up.
mobileWake.holdHint: Longest the caller waits for the phone to wake and re-register. 8 to 30.
mobileWake.settleHint: Extra wait after the re-registration so the app is ready to ring. 0 to 10.
mobileWake.markerHint: Text in the SIP User-Agent that marks a mobile client, so a desk phone on the same extension does not count as the phone waking up. Contacts with RFC 8599 pn-* parameters always count.
